title: EIP-8456: CALLSTATUS instruction
description: Instruction that returns whether the last call of the frame succeeded, reverted or halted, and whether a halt occurred below it
author: Stavros Vlachakis (@svlachakis)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract This EIP adds the `CALLSTATUS` instruction. It pushes the completion status of the most recent `CALL`, `CALLCODE`, `DELEGATECALL`, `STATICCALL`, `CREATE` or `CREATE2` executed in the current frame, as three bits: whether the callee reverted, whether it halted exceptionally or failed consuming its gas, and whether such a failure occurred in a frame below the callee. The values are `0` (success), `1` (reverted or not started), `2` (halted exceptionally, or collided), `4` (succeeded after a halt below) and `5` (reverted after a halt below). A value of `2` or more means that gas forwarded somewhere in the line of the call, if any, was consumed by an exceptional halt or an address collision. The instruction reads a per-frame register, pops nothing, and costs 2 gas. ## Motivation A contract that continues after a failed call needs to know why the call failed. A failure that the callee signalled with `REVERT` can be recorded as final. A failure caused by too little gas must not be, because the transaction sender controls the gas and can use an underfunded call to make the contract record a false failure, for example to burn a retry or to mark a payment as rejected. Today the EVM gives the caller no direct evidence of the cause. The caller sees a success flag of `0`, the return data, and the gas it has left. Contracts therefore infer the cause from gas arithmetic: they compare `GAS` after the call with a threshold derived from the gas they forwarded, or they rely on the failure handler itself running out of gas. Such checks hold only under assumptions about the gas schedule: that an exceptional halt consumes all forwarded gas, that no gas returns to the caller before the check, and that the costs of the operations in the handler do not change. Each repricing fork has broken thresholds of this kind, and the separate metering of state creation, with gas that a frame can draw from a transaction-wide reservoir, weakens `GAS` further as evidence of what happened in the callee. Return data does not help either: a `REVERT` with no data and an exceptional halt both leave empty return data, and a wrapper that reverts with a reason after a failed call hides the halt behind the reason. The EVM knows at every frame boundary whether the frame halted, and it can carry that fact up through the frames above, whether they revert, return, or handle the failure and go on. `CALLSTATUS` exposes it, so that a contract can treat a status of `2` or more as "not final" and stop depending on the gas schedule. ## Specification ### Parameters | Constant | Value | |---|---| | `CALLSTATUS_OPCODE` | `0xA5` | | `CALLSTATUS_GAS` | `2` | ### Status values A status is the sum of up to three bits: | Bit | Value | Meaning | |---|---|---| | 0 | `1` | the operation reverted, or was not started and returned its gas | | 1 | `2` | the operation halted exceptionally, or failed in a way that consumed the gas it would have forwarded | | 2 | `4` | an operation in a frame below halted exceptionally or had an address collision | The values that occur are `0`, `1`, `2`, `4` and `5`. Bit 1 is never combined with another bit. ### Per-frame registers Every frame of execution has a register `call_status`, initialised to `0`, and a flag `halt_seen`, initialised to `false`, when the frame starts. `DELEGATECALL` and `CALLCODE` start a frame of their own, with its own registers, like `CALL`, `STATICCALL`, `CREATE` and `CREATE2`. The registers of a frame are not visible to, and not changed by, the execution of any other frame, except as stated below for the completion of a child frame. At the completion of each `CALL` (`0xF1`), `CALLCODE` (`0xF2`), `DELEGATECALL` (`0xF4`), `STATICCALL` (`0xFA`), `CREATE` (`0xF0`) and `CREATE2` (`0xF5`) instruction, the executing frame sets `call_status` to: - `1` if no child frame was started because the operation failed before it, and the gas that would have been forwarded is returned: insufficient balance for the value transfer or the endowment, the call depth limit, or, for `CREATE` and `CREATE2`, a nonce overflow of the creating account. - `2` if, for `CREATE` and `CREATE2`, no child frame was started because of an address collision, which is checked only after the conditions above. The gas that would have been forwarded is consumed. - `2` if a child frame was started and halted exceptionally, whatever the cause: out of gas, an invalid instruction, an invalid jump destination, a stack underflow or overflow, a write in a static context, an out-of-bounds return data access, a precompiled contract that fails, and, for `CREATE` and `CREATE2`, a failed code deposit. The gas forwarded to the child frame is consumed. - `1` if a child frame was started and completed with `REVERT`, and the child's `halt_seen` is `false`. - `5` if a child frame was started and completed with `REVERT`, and the child's `halt_seen` is `true`. - `0` if a child frame was started and completed successfully, and the child's `halt_seen` is `false`. Successful completion is `STOP`, `RETURN` or `SELFDESTRUCT`, running past the end of the code, executing no code because the target has none or is delegated to a precompiled contract, or, for a call to a precompiled contract, completing without error. For `CREATE` and `CREATE2`, success includes the code deposit. - `4` if a child frame was started and completed successfully, and the child's `halt_seen` is `true`. After setting `call_status`, the executing frame sets `halt_seen` to `true` if `call_status` is `2` or more. `halt_seen` is never set back to `false`. A child that halted exceptionally reports `2` whatever its own registers hold. A precompiled contract runs no calls, so its `halt_seen` is `false`. If the instruction halts the executing frame itself, for example a `CALL` with value in a static context, insufficient gas for the memory expansion, or initcode longer than the limit, the frame ends and its registers have no further effect.
